newsitem.title: NAMIBIA: GM plant in Namibia operational by November.
newsitem.headline: GM plant in Namibia operational by November.

text.p: Namibia's General Motors assembly plant is expected to be operational by November this year, a spokesman said on Wednesday.

"The plant should be operational by the beginning of November, the corporate headquarters and retail dealership will still be in construction for another eight weeks," Audley Smith, Managing Director of Barden International in Windhoek told Reuters.
"We expect production to start in full force in January," he added.
The Namibian government and Barden International, a Detroit-based company, signed a deal on the setting up of a General Motors assembly and conversion plant in December 1996.
Smith said building would be completed by mid-October.
About US$19 million has been invested in building the plant and training staff.
Barden International hopes to have 40 GM vehicles a month rolling out of the plant, which will initially provide only for the Namibian market.
General Motors already has operational passenger and light-duty truck assembly plants in Nigeria, Kenya, Tunisia and Egypt.
GM's fleet sales manager for Africa operations, Joe Parker, said there would be no conflict of interest between operations in Botswana and Namibia.
"In Botswana they assemble medium-duty trucks (over five tonnes), and in Namibia they will be assembling light-duty trucks (under five tonnes) upfitting conversion," Parker told Reuters.
"There is no conflict on sales and distributions, since they are two different product lines, two different processes," Parker said.
"Both the Botswana and the Namibian operations are part of GM's plans to harmonise product lines," he said, adding that so far the Botswana operation was doing well in meeting GM standards.
